title: Choose the visual world for lee.sh
question: The roll assigned the Cyanotype Drawing Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cyanotype Drawing Sheet
options.lineage: engineering blueprints: cyanotype drawing sheets with zone borders, title blocks and detail views
options.thesis: The board is drawn as an engineering drawing: every part is lettered with its facts.
options.viewport: One full sheet: the board in plan view, lettered parts, zone border A–F / 1–8, and a title block bottom-right that answers the recruiter: LEE, Senior Backend Engineer, stack, OPEN TO ROLES, résumé.
options.risk: Blueprint is a known web trope; it only works if it follows real drafting convention (zones, detail views, scale notes), not a grid-paper theme.

raised.raise: The name in the title block is set at true display scale, the loudest mark on the sheet.
State by inversion: a selected part fills solid white with blue lettering, with no glow and no colour shift.
One lettering family for the whole sheet; hierarchy comes only from size, case and weight.
Every sheet is composed on the CPU's chain-line centre axes; each detail view aligns to them.
Every drawn part carries lettering. An unlabelled part is cut.

options.label: The Datasheet
options.lineage: semiconductor datasheets: front page, features list, pinout, block diagram
options.thesis: Lee is published as a part: LEE-5Y, Senior Backend Engineer, with a pinout where every pin name is a fact.
options.viewport: Datasheet page 1: red band with part number LEE-5Y, Features and Applications lists in the left column, and the CPU pinout at full size on the right with pins named Python, Django and so on.
options.risk: The most familiar form for this audience. Datasheet prose tends to pull facts into columns beside the part, away from the component.

options.label: Assembly Manual
options.lineage: brick build-instruction books, fused with motherboard install guides
options.thesis: Scrolling assembles the board one numbered step at a time, and each part lands carrying its facts.
options.viewport: Step 1: a huge numeral, a parts inventory box, the bare board ghosted, and the CPU dropping along a dashed arrow into its socket, its lid lettered LEE.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the scroll order becomes the build order and prior parts ghost like depth of field. It holds product clarity but loses audience identification, because the toy register undercuts 'senior'.
options.risk: Reads playful; a senior backend hiring panel may file it as whimsy.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The board printed as a live transcript.
options.risk: A terminal-only page is on the rejected list.
options.case: Fails product truth: a terminal-only page is permanently rejected, and it loses the hardware drawing.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Each part opens as a window.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows over a dithered desktop.
options.risk: Window chrome competes with the board.
options.case: Loses both axes: desktop windows aren't hardware, and the chrome buries the parts.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: The board as an axial garden plan.
options.viewport: A parterre plan with the CPU as the palace.
options.case: Loses both axes: neither audience sees itself in a garden.

options.label: Street Typography
options.viewport: Diagonal stacked capitals cropped by the frame.
options.case: Loses both axes: too loud for Lee, and the parts disappear under the type.
options.kept: Courage of scale on the name.

options.label: Magazine Density
options.viewport: Overlapping parts tagged on leader lines.
options.risk: Floating call-outs are the rejected 'separate info' pattern.
options.case: Loses both axes: leader-line tags move the information off the components.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer-portfolio standard, done impeccably: dark ground, one accent, glowing traces.
canonCard.viewport: Close to the current pages, tightened and polished.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from most dark developer portfolios by design.
